description: Constructing, modifying, analyzing and visualizing graphs: vertices and edges, adjacency and incidence representations, paths and distances, centrality measures, connectivity, cycles and trees, community detection, and standard parameterized graph families.

tools.name: Graph
tools.description: Constructs a graph from a list of edges, or from vertices together with edges, with extensive styling and annotation options. Both directed and undirected edges are supported, as are edge weights and vertex properties. It is the central object that all graph functions operate on.

parameters.name: EdgeWeight
parameters.description: List of numeric weights, used by distance and flow functions.

tools.notes: UndirectedEdge is written as a <-> b or UndirectedEdge[a, b]; DirectedEdge as a -> b.

tools.name: DirectedEdge
tools.description: Represents a directed edge from one vertex to another, normally written with the arrow shorthand a -> b inside a graph. Direction matters for reachability, flow and centrality computations. Mixed graphs may contain both directed and undirected edges.

tools.name: UndirectedEdge
tools.description: Represents an undirected edge between two vertices, written with the shorthand a <-> b. Undirected graphs are the default for many constructors such as CompleteGraph. Use it explicitly when mixing edge types.

tools.name: VertexList
tools.description: Returns the list of vertices of a graph, optionally restricted to those matching a pattern. The order it returns is the canonical order used by matrix representations. Use it to align external data with adjacency matrices.

tools.name: EdgeList
tools.description: Returns the list of edges of a graph, optionally filtered by a pattern. Edges come back as DirectedEdge or UndirectedEdge expressions. Use it for serialization and for iterating over connections.

tools.name: AdjacencyMatrix
tools.description: Returns the adjacency matrix of a graph as a SparseArray, with rows and columns ordered as in VertexList. It is the bridge from graph structure to linear algebra. Use it for spectral methods and matrix-based algorithms.
tools.notes: WeightedAdjacencyMatrix uses edge weights instead of ones; AdjacencyGraph converts back.

tools.name: AdjacencyGraph
tools.description: Builds a graph from an adjacency matrix, optionally with explicit vertex names. Nonzero entries become edges, and the matrix symmetry determines directedness unless specified. Use it to import graphs from numeric data.

tools.name: IncidenceMatrix
tools.description: Returns the vertex-edge incidence matrix of a graph as a SparseArray. For directed graphs entries are signed to indicate tail and head. It is used in network flow formulations and algebraic graph theory.

tools.name: FindShortestPath
tools.description: Finds a shortest path between two vertices, or a function giving shortest paths from one source. Edge weights are respected, with Dijkstra and Bellman-Ford methods available. Use it for routing and reachability analysis.
tools.usage:
FindShortestPath[g, s, t]
FindShortestPath[g, s, All]
FindShortestPath[g, All, All]
tools.notes: FindShortestPath[g, s, All] returns a reusable function, which is much faster for many queries.

tools.name: GraphDistance
tools.description: Gives the length of a shortest path between two vertices, or the distances from one vertex to all others. Edge weights are used when present. Use it when only the distance, not the path, is needed.
tools.notes: GraphDistanceMatrix returns all pairwise distances at once.

tools.name: BetweennessCentrality
tools.description: Measures how often each vertex lies on shortest paths between other vertices. High values identify bridges and bottlenecks in a network. Use it to find critical routers, brokers or chokepoints.
tools.notes: EdgeBetweennessCentrality does the same for edges and underlies the Girvan-Newman community algorithm.

tools.name: ClosenessCentrality
tools.description: Measures how close each vertex is to all others, as the reciprocal of its average shortest-path distance. High values indicate vertices that can reach the whole network quickly. Use it to find well-positioned hubs.

tools.name: PageRankCentrality
tools.description: Computes PageRank scores, the stationary distribution of a random surfer that follows edges with a damping probability. It rewards vertices pointed to by other important vertices. Use it for ranking in directed networks such as web or citation graphs.

tools.name: DegreeCentrality
tools.description: Gives the number of edges incident to each vertex, with options to count only incoming or outgoing edges. It is the simplest and fastest centrality measure. Use it as a first look at which vertices are locally important.

tools.name: EigenvectorCentrality
tools.description: Scores vertices by the principal eigenvector of the adjacency matrix, so that connections to high-scoring vertices count more. It captures global influence better than raw degree. Use it for social influence and spectral ranking.

tools.name: VertexDegree
tools.description: Returns the degree of each vertex, or of a specified vertex. VertexInDegree and VertexOutDegree give the directed variants. It is the basic structural statistic of a graph.

tools.name: ConnectedComponents
tools.description: Returns the connected components of a graph as lists of vertices, using strong connectivity for directed graphs. It is the standard way to detect disconnected parts of a network. WeaklyConnectedComponents ignores edge direction.

tools.name: FindCycle
tools.description: Finds cycles in a graph, with control over their length and how many to return. It is used for detecting feedback loops and circular dependencies. Returning All finds every cycle within the length bounds.

tools.name: FindHamiltonianCycle
tools.description: Finds a cycle that visits every vertex exactly once, if one exists. The problem is NP-hard, so this is practical only for modest graphs. Use it for tour construction and combinatorial puzzles.
tools.notes: FindHamiltonianPath drops the requirement to return to the start; FindShortestTour solves the weighted travelling-salesman version.

tools.name: FindEulerianCycle
tools.description: Finds a closed walk that uses every edge exactly once, if the graph admits one. Existence requires all degrees to be even in the connected case. Use it for route planning where every link must be traversed.

tools.name: FindSpanningTree
tools.description: Finds a minimum spanning tree of a weighted graph, or a spanning forest for disconnected graphs. It also accepts a list of points and builds the Euclidean minimum spanning tree. Use it for network design and clustering.
tools.example:
g = RandomGraph[{20, 60}, EdgeWeight -> RandomReal[1, 60]];
HighlightGraph[g, FindSpanningTree[g]]

tools.name: TopologicalSort
tools.description: Returns an ordering of the vertices of a directed acyclic graph in which every edge points forward. It fails if the graph contains a cycle. Use it for dependency resolution, build ordering and scheduling.

tools.name: FindMaximumFlow
tools.description: Computes the maximum flow from a source to a sink in a capacitated network, returning the value or the flow assignment. Capacities come from edge weights or an explicit specification. Use it for bottleneck and matching problems.
tools.usage:
FindMaximumFlow[g, s, t]
FindMaximumFlow[g, s, t, "OptimumFlowData"]
tools.notes: FindMinimumCostFlow handles costs as well as capacities.

tools.name: FindGraphCommunities
tools.description: Partitions a graph into communities of densely connected vertices using modularity optimization or other methods. It returns lists of vertices, one per community. Use it to find modules in social, biological or technical networks.

tools.name: CommunityGraphPlot
tools.description: Draws a graph with its communities visually grouped and shaded. Communities can be supplied explicitly or detected automatically. Use it to present modular structure clearly.

tools.name: HighlightGraph
tools.description: Draws a graph with specified vertices, edges or subgraphs highlighted in a distinct style. It is the standard way to display algorithm results such as paths, trees and communities. Multiple highlight groups can be styled separately.

tools.name: Subgraph
tools.description: Extracts the subgraph induced by a given set of vertices or edges, keeping all properties. It is the basic way to restrict analysis to part of a network. Options can restyle the result.

tools.name: NeighborhoodGraph
tools.description: Returns the subgraph consisting of a vertex, the vertices within a given distance of it, and the edges among them. It is the natural way to inspect a local region of a large network. The radius defaults to one.

tools.name: VertexDelete
tools.description: Removes vertices, and the edges incident to them, from a graph. Patterns can be used to delete whole classes of vertices. Use it for pruning and for robustness experiments.
tools.notes: VertexAdd, EdgeAdd and EdgeDelete perform the complementary modifications.

tools.name: EdgeAdd
tools.description: Adds edges to an existing graph, creating any vertices that do not yet exist. It returns a new graph, leaving the original unchanged. Use it to build graphs incrementally.

tools.name: EdgeDelete
tools.description: Removes specified edges from a graph while keeping all vertices. Patterns select classes of edges to remove. Use it for percolation studies and for cutting links.

tools.name: GraphPlot
tools.description: Draws a graph using a chosen layout algorithm, with full control over vertex and edge rendering. It accepts a Graph object, a list of rules, or an adjacency matrix. Use it when you want layout control beyond the default rendering of Graph.
tools.notes: LayeredGraphPlot and TreePlot are specialized for hierarchies; GraphPlot3D lays out in three dimensions.

tools.name: LayeredGraphPlot
tools.description: Draws a directed graph in layers so that edges flow consistently in one direction. It is ideal for dependency graphs, flowcharts and hierarchies. Layer direction and spacing can be set.

tools.name: CompleteGraph
tools.description: Generates the complete graph on n vertices, in which every pair is connected. With a list argument it generates complete multipartite graphs. Use it as a dense test case and as a building block.

tools.name: GridGraph
tools.description: Generates a rectangular grid graph of the given dimensions, in any number of dimensions. Periodic wrapping can be requested to build torus graphs. Use it for lattice models and mesh-like networks.

tools.name: RandomGraph
tools.description: Generates random graphs from a specified model, most commonly a fixed number of vertices and edges. Named distributions such as BarabasiAlbertGraphDistribution and WattsStrogatzGraphDistribution are also accepted. Use it for null models and algorithm testing.
tools.usage:
RandomGraph[{n, m}]
RandomGraph[{n, m}, k]
RandomGraph[gdist]

tools.name: PathGraph
tools.description: Generates a graph that is a simple path through the given vertices in order. It is the simplest connected graph family. Use it to represent chains, routes and sequences.

tools.name: CycleGraph
tools.description: Generates the cycle graph on n vertices, a single closed ring. It is a standard test graph with known spectral properties. Use it for periodic structures and ring topologies.

tools.name: KaryTree
tools.description: Generates a complete k-ary tree with a given number of vertices, binary by default. Directed or undirected forms are available. Use it for hierarchical test structures and tree algorithms.
tools.notes: Related families: StarGraph, WheelGraph, CompleteKaryTree, TorusGraph, HypercubeGraph.

tools.name: IsomorphicGraphQ
tools.description: Tests whether two graphs are isomorphic, that is identical up to renaming of vertices. FindGraphIsomorphism returns the actual vertex mapping. Use it to detect duplicate structures and canonical forms.
